Restore an archived run

Source: R/archive.R
restore_run.Rd

Writes the archived copies of a run's files under to, recreating the run's folder layout, so the run can be inspected or rerun. No existing file is overwritten.

Usage

restore_run(
  run_id,
  to,
  project = TRUE,
  model = FALSE,
  data = FALSE,
  outputs = TRUE,
  config = FALSE,
  store = default_store(),
  archive = NULL
)

Arguments

run_id

Character scalar. The run to restore; it must have been archived with archive_run().

to

Character scalar. The folder to restore into; created if needed.

project, model, data, outputs, config

Logical scalars. Which groups of files to restore.

store

Character scalar. The run store directory (see default_store()). Defaults to default_store().

archive

Character scalar or NULL. The folder that holds the objects folder, when it has moved since the run was archived. NULL (the default) uses the location the manifest records.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with one row per restored file and per model or data file left out, with columns group, path (the file's original path), restored_to (NA when not restored) and status: "restored", or for a model or data file left out "not_restored_current_matches", "not_restored_current_differs" or "not_restored_current_missing" (no file at the original path now).

Details

Files are grouped as: project (the project file), model (inputs of role "model"; Monolix library models lib: are not files and are not archived), data (every other input except the config file: data, regressors, doses, external files), outputs (recorded outputs) and config (the config file input and the copy of the tool's config.ini). By default the project and outputs are restored and the model and data are not, since those are often shared files maintained elsewhere; for each model or data file left out, a message says whether the file now at its original path matches the archived copy.

Where: a file recorded relative to the store's folder goes to the same relative path under to, so the restored project's references to files under the store's folder resolve to the restored copies. A file recorded with an absolute path (outside the store's folder) goes under to/_absolute/, a Windows drive letter becoming a folder (e.g. _absolute/C/data/pk.csv); the project file is not rewritten, so it still references the original path, and a warning names each such file and where its archived copy was written. The config.ini copy goes to <to>/config.ini.

Before anything is written, every chosen object is checked against its recorded SHA-256 and every target path must be free: to may exist, but no file to restore may already be there. On any problem nothing is written and the error names the file.

Called interactively with none of project, model, data, outputs and config given, a menu lists each group with its number of files and size (and, for model and data, whether the current file matches), the default groups marked (default). Nothing is preselected; selecting nothing restores nothing.

The archive is found where the run's manifest records it; pass archive when it has moved. When the archive folder does not exist the error names it.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
run_id <- run_status("base/run3.mlxtran")$run_id
restore_run(run_id, "restored/run3")
restore_run(run_id, "restored/run3-full", model = TRUE, data = TRUE, config = TRUE)
} # }
